q0AnchorReason: Reads no q0. Checks 1-3 are exact rational identities over AME2020 binding energies; check 4 evaluates one hand-chosen exponential member. No substrate quantity enters, so neither the convention-C/D question nor the q0 pin can move the payload. The witness carries no q0 field.
description: The linear-minus-concave-deficit class Phi = c*x - a*psi(x), psi concave -- the class qou-zy94 proposed to exclude -- cannot be excluded by three points, because membership follows from the convexity the same points establish. Shown two ways: exactly, via det3 = 0 for every data-derived psi over an open ray of c; and by an explicit member with INCREASING local exponent, which refutes the proposed monotone-exponent route directly.
q0_pin: not applicable -- consumes no framework quantity

assertions.name: the AME grid is convex through the origin (the antecedent of the Lean theorem holds on the corpus's own numbers)
for EVERY c above the top secant slope the deficit is concave through the origin AND strictly increasing -- an open ray of witnesses, not a lucky one

det3(x, psi, Phi) = 0 EXACTLY for every data-derived psi, so the AggregatorFamilyExclusions filter returns 'consistent' on the class -- its five nonzero determinants are about parameter counting, not about the concave-deficit structure
the monotone-exponent hypothesis is FALSE on the class: the member c*x - a*(1 - exp(-x/L)) is convex through the origin with a concave increasing deficit and INCREASING secant exponents

CAVEAT ASSERTED: that member carries THREE parameters (c, a, L) on three points, so it is underdetermined and untestable here -- it refutes the monotonicity hypothesis and is NOT evidence that it fits

scope: (b) for the proposed exclusion route -- the invariant is the slope-negation identity proved in QOU.MassTheory.ConcaveDeficitNonExclusion, not cited. It excludes no aggregator; it excludes a METHOD of excluding aggregators.
caveats: This says nothing about which psi is right. A FIXED shape remains testable by det3, and all five shapes tried in aggregator_family_exclusion_probe.py are still excluded. Do not read this as reopening those.

The exponential member has three parameters on three points and is therefore UNDERDETERMINED, hence untestable here -- exactly the regime the SEMF caveat in the sibling probe describes. Exhibiting it refutes the monotonicity hypothesis; it is NOT a candidate fit.
The monotone-exponent hypothesis IS true for psi(x) = x^s, where it was read off. What fails is its generalisation to the class.
Three points are three points. This is a statement about what this grid can decide; extending it past A = 4 with a DERIVED bond set is what would change it.
